messages:
olivia: Quick ping — opened PR #4325 to refactor the request serializer into smaller modules. It's mostly cleanup and moving functions out of serializers.py into serializers/core.py, serializers/json.py, serializers/compat.py. Need a couple of experienced eyes for style/modular boundaries before I merge. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4325

mason: Thanks — can you summarize public API changes?

olivia: No public API changes other than renaming serialize_request -> serialize (internal use). Left a deprecation shim for one release. Tests updated. See CHANGELOG fragment in PR.

liam: I'll take a look in a bit. Any behavior diffs in edge cases?

olivia: I ran full unit + integration locally. Found one subtle order-of-kwargs change in header serialization — added regression test. But would like to confirm I didn't inadvertently leak internal helpers in __init__ exports.

sophia: tagging @mason because he owns high-level serializer usage in client runtime. Also +1 for not changing public names if avoidable.

mason: grabbing now. quick heads up — if you moved helpers, please check import cycles, we had one in eng-runtime last year.

olivia: Good call, I ran flake8 import-order checks, but didn't catch runtime cycles; CI includes import-linter but it's flaky. If you see import loop, suggest moving compat helpers into runtime/utils.

ci-bot: CI started for PR #4325 — all tests running.

liam: scanning files — style nits: trailing commas in some multi-line dicts, docstring format inconsistent (numpydoc vs Google). I'd prefer Google; can you align or drop numpydoc note?

olivia: willing to align to Google, but that's a broader repo standard. For this PR I'll normalize only in changed files. If that's ok, I can run ruff autofix and black.

sophia: that's fine. also check that new modules have __all__ defined to control public symbols.

mason: looked at exports — one helper _format_header is not underscore-prefixed anymore. Please make it private.

olivia: will change. Also: should we add a small module-level docstring explaining intent of each submodule? helps future reviewers.

liam: yes please.

mason: CI passed unit tests so far, integration queued. If no other objections I'll merge after the few small edits (make helper private, docs). :thumbsup:

olivia: thanks all — I'll push changes in ~20m. If anyone wants to take a second pass post-push, ping me.
